name: nfcutils
desc: Near Field Communication (NFC) tools under POSIX systems
why: NFC tools that read and write tags from a reader, a real door into the hidden protocols in cards and transit passes.

brief.what_it_is: nfcutils is described as a set of Near Field Communication (NFC) tools for POSIX systems. Its one listed executable is lsnfc. From the formula description alone, it appears to be command-line utilities that talk to NFC hardware. I could not read the README, so I cannot confirm what it takes in or what it outputs. The scout note says it reads and writes tags from a reader, but that is unverified.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew under the formula name nfcutils. The formula lists no caveats. I could not read the README, so I have no details on hardware readers, libraries, or first-run configuration.
brief.standout: Unverified. The scout note suggests it is a practical way to inspect NFC cards and transit passes from a POSIX shell, but I could not confirm this from the project's own pages.
brief.status: unknown. Both fetches of the GitHub repository returned no content, so I found no release date, commit date, or maintenance note.
brief.caveats: The homepage was unreachable. Both fetch attempts to https://github.com/nfc-tools/nfcutils returned empty output, so this brief rests only on the formula description and scout notes. Nothing here has been checked against the README. The scout note's claims about reading and writing tags and about transit-pass protocols are unverified. Any entry should treat them as unconfirmed.
